## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of container runtimes and correctness of patching deployments are critical in real-world CKAD tasks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities drop
- Probes: readiness and liveness on /healthz
- Deployment strategy: RollingUpdate for zero-downtime upgrades
- Validation: load testing, rollout status, and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: portal
  namespace: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: portal
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: portal
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.25
        ports:
``` 

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your understanding of namespace-scoped automation, PVC usage, and secure scanning workflows within Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace CronJob with PVC mounts for manifests and logs
- Lightweight containerized scanner (e.g., trivy-lite)
- ConfigMap-based findings storage
- InitContainer for tool provisioning (jq, curl)
- Readiness and liveness probes on Job Pods
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress restrictions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: manifest-scan
  namespace: example-ns
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: tools-installer
            image: busybox:1.36
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              wget -q https://github.com/stedolan/jq/releases/download/jq-1.6/jq-linux64 -O /tmp/jq
              chmod +x /tmp/jq
              apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tmp
          containers:
          - name: scanner
            image: trivy-lite:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: manifests
              mountPath: /manifests
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              export PATH=/tmp:$PATH
              for manifest in /manifests/*.yaml; do
                trivy scan --format json -o /logs/$(basename $manifest).json $manifest
              done
              kubectl get configmap security-scan -n example-ns -o yaml > /logs/configmap-backup.yaml
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - ls
                - /logs
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - cat
                - /tmp/health
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: manifests
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: manifest-pvc
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: log-pvc
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs ConfigMap**: Using a PVC for logs allows for larger log volumes and retention, but requires storage provisioning. ConfigMaps are simpler but size-limited.
- **InitContainer vs Sidecar**: InitContainers run once per pod startup; sidecars run continuously. For a CronJob, InitContainers are more cost-effective.
- **NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress improves security but may break updates if registries change. Consider using DNS whitelisting rather than specific IP ranges.
- **Probe timing**: Aggressive probes may cause premature failures; conservative settings increase job execution time.
- **CronJob frequency**: More frequent scans catch vulnerabilities faster but increase cluster load and API calls.

It also exercises InitContainers, probes, and network policy considerations in a real workflow.

- Patching Deployment images with kubectl set image or patch
- Reading image tag from ConfigMap and registry authentication via Secret
- Persisting status in a ConfigMap and logging to a PVC
- InitContainer to install tooling (kubectl, jq)
- Readiness/Liveness probes for the Job Pod
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting registry egress

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-upgrade
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq; true"]
            volumeMounts:
```
